symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two input integers, a count of bits.
symbols.quote: Here $n$ is the number of bits in each of the two input integers.

symbols.name: big-O bound
symbols.meaning: The asymptotic upper bound: a function is O(g) when it is at most a constant times g for all large inputs.
symbols.quote: Here $O(g)$ means at most a constant times $g$ for all large inputs.

symbols.name: binary logarithm
symbols.meaning: The base-2 logarithm rounded up and at least 1, so that lg n = max{ceil(log2 n), 1}.
symbols.quote: The logarithm $\lg n = \max\{\lceil \log_2 n\rceil, 1\}$ is the base-2 logarithm rounded up and at least 1.

symbols.name: power-saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^(-182) by which the power of lg n falls below one.
symbols.quote: The constant $\kappa = 2^{-182}$ is the power-saving exponent, the fixed amount by which the power of $\lg n$ falls below one.

relations.quote: The result disproves the [Schönhage–Strassen n log n conjecture](nlogn-conjecture.md).
Polynomial products are computed by [signed Kronecker packing](kronecker-packing.md) and the [Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) multiplication](harvey-hoeven-multiplier.md).
The power saving follows from [Recursive power saving](recursive-power-saving.md), so both tape procedures save a power of their parameter, with exponent strictly below one.
The product is reduced to the carried convolution of the digit sequences, as in [Multiplication as convolution of digits](convolution-reduction.md).
The digit list is placed by the [Chinese-remainder address map](chinese-remainder-address-map.md) on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes.
The multiplier computes its transforms by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), which expresses a prime-length transform through power-of-two axes.
The middle transform is converted by [Bluestein's chirp identity](bluestein-chirp.md) into a normalized cyclic convolution.
The last cyclic coordinate is handled in the [polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$](polynomial-ring-y.md), so that its wrap is a signed shift.
The two forward transforms are carried out by the [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md), which keeps frequency order through the pointwise product.
Each transform level is built from [simultaneous butterfly layers](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md), each acting on one address bit.
The address permutations are performed by [fast address interchange](address-interchange.md).
The exact product is recovered by [exact recovery by rounding](rounding-recovery.md): the coefficient error is below $1/2$, so rounding and carries give the binary product.
